Incremental Theory and One-trial Theory present contrasting views on learning processes in
cognitive and motor tasks. Incremental Theory is predominantly supported in cognitive
tasks, where knowledge and skills are acquired gradually through practice and experience,
emphasizing that intelligence and abilities can develop over time. Conversely, One-trial
Theory is more applicable to motor tasks, where learning can occur effectively after a
single exposure or practice session, as seen in skills like riding a bike or throwing a
ball. These theories have significant implications for educational practices; educators
might focus on fostering continuous learning and resilience in cognitive areas, while
emphasizing immediate practice and feedback in motor skill development. Understanding
these distinctions can help tailor teaching strategies to optimize learning outcomes in
different domains.
answers.explanation: The answer correctly identifies that Incremental Theory emphasizes gradual skill development in cognitive tasks, while One-trial Theory highlights the effectiveness of single-exposure learning in motor tasks, reflecting their distinct implications for educational practices.

Providing education and job training to adolescents and young adults post-drug treatment
exemplifies secondary intervention in psychological support by addressing the needs of
individuals who are at a heightened risk of relapse or social reintegration challenges.
Secondary intervention focuses on early detection and preventive measures to reduce the
severity of issues that may arise after treatment. By equipping these young individuals
with skills and knowledge, we not only enhance their employability but also promote self-
efficacy and social integration, which are crucial for maintaining recovery. This approach
can significantly decrease the likelihood of returning to substance use, ultimately
fostering a more supportive environment for sustained mental health and well-being.
Therefore, education and job training serve as vital components of a comprehensive
strategy to mitigate the risks associated with post-treatment vulnerabilities.
